summary: This note covers Atlanta's role in the American Civil War, focusing on the 1864 Union invasion of the city. It describes several battles fought in the area that is now metropolitan Atlanta, and the Confederate evacuation of the city in September 1864 after a siege by Union forces.
one_line: Overview of Atlanta's 1864 Union invasion and the battles fought around the city during the American Civil War.
key_facts: In 1864, Atlanta became the target of a major Union invasion, as had been feared by Jeremy F. Gilmer.
The area now covered by metropolitan Atlanta was the scene of several fiercely contested battles.
The Battle of Peachtree Creek, the Battle of Atlanta, Battle of Ezra Church and the Battle of Jonesboro were fought in the Atlanta area.
On September 1, 1864, Confederate Gen. John Bell Hood evacuated Atlanta.
Confederate Gen. John Bell Hood's evacuation of Atlanta followed a five-week siege mounted by Union Gen. William Sherman.
Confederate Gen. John Bell Hood ordered all public buildings and possible Confederate assets in Atlanta destroyed when he evacuated the city.
Jeremy F. Gilmer had feared that Atlanta would become the target of a Union invasion in 1864.
